Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Agency on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter within its
jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address the
Agency, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms.
The Agency will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Agency will
hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency
or special circumstances exist. The Agency may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future
Agency meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Agency:
  ♦ Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  ♦ Comments should be directed to the Agency as a whole and not directed to individual Agency Members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other
services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time
when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Agency regarding any item on this agenda after it has been posted
will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular
business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720.
You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE NORWALK REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  FEBRUARY 4, 2020

Chair Rios called the regular meeting to order at 6:13 p.m. in Council Chambers, Norwalk

entirety with Board Members Ayala, Perez, and Shryock, Vice Chair Vernola, and Chair
Rios responding to roll call. Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, Executive Director;
Arnold M. Alvarez-Glasman, Agency Counsel; and Theresa Devoy, Secretary.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one
motion and roll call vote. Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and
considered separately by the Agency. Chair Rios moved and Board Member Perez
seconded to approve the consent calendar as recommended. MOTION CARRIED BY
THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Board Members Ayala, Perez, and Shryock, Vice Chair Vernola, and
  Chair Rios

ABSENT:  None

The Agency approved the minutes of the regular meetings of December 3 and 17,
2019.  1305-03

WARRANTS

The Agency approved the warrant registers for the period November 27, 2019 –
December 24, 2019, in the total amount of $56,387.50 and January 15, 2020 – January
29, 2020, in the total amount of $54,937.50.  1310-01

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR’S REPORT

The City Manager thanked staff for the timely submission of the Recognized Obligation
Payment Schedule (ROPS), which was approved by the County.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There were no persons wishing to address the Agency.

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, Executive Director

BY:  Theresa Devoy, CMC, City Clerk

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. SA 20-01 - FACSIMILE SIGNATURES

Background:

Government Code §5501 provides that any authorized officer may, after filing with the
Secretary of State his manual signature certified by him under oath, execute or cause to
be executed, certain documents including any instrument of payment, with a facsimile
signature in lieu of a manual signature. Following the filing of the facsimile signature with
the Secretary of State, banks may be directed to honor all checks, drafts, and warrants
when bearing those signatures and facsimile signatures.

This resolution authorizes banks to honor checks, drafts and warrants bearing the manual
or facsimile signatures of Chair Perez plus the manual or facsimile signature of Jana
Stuard, Finance Officer.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Board of Directors adopt Resolution No. SA 20-01, authorizing and
directing certain banks to honor all checks, drafts, and warrants when bearing certain
signatures and facsimile signatures of agency officials and rescinding all previous
resolutions.
